items.quote: Concept 1 · Coordinate Geometry Basics
items.text: Concept 1 · Coordinate Geometry Basics

items.quote: Find the coordinates of the division point (internal and external)
items.text: Learning Outcomes: Find the coordinates of the division point (internal and external) of a line segment on the number line.

items.quote: When a surgeon plans a minimally invasive robotic surgery
items.text: Intro: a surgeon's robotic arm must navigate 3D space inside the body to target a tumor without damaging tissue; imaging software maps anatomy onto a precise grid, each landmark given numerical coordinates, so the system determines optimal paths, distances and boundary midpoints.

items.quote: How does mapping physical space onto a grid of numbers allow
items.text: How does mapping physical space onto a grid of numbers allow us to precisely partition paths, find balances, and safely navigate complex physical environments?

items.quote: On a number line, one real number a corresponds to point P.
items.claim: On a number line, one real number $a$ corresponds to point P; $a$ is called the coordinate of P, and P with coordinate $a$ is denoted P($a$).

items.quote: The distance AB between two points A(a) and B(b)
items.claim: The distance AB between A($a$) and B($b$) on a number line is given by AB = |b − a|. Side note: since distance cannot be negative, we use the absolute value.

items.quote: point P is said to divide the line segment AB internally in the ratio
items.claim: If P is on segment AB such that AP:PB = m : n, P is said to divide AB internally in the ratio m : n.

items.quote: point Q is said to divide the line segment AB externally in the ratio
items.claim: If Q is on the extension of segment AB such that AQ:QB = m : n, Q is said to divide AB externally in the ratio m : n.

items.quote: Point P is a point m away from A and n away from B.
items.caption: Two number lines with arrow labelled x. Top: A(a), P, B(b), with arcs m (A to P) and n (P to B); caption 'Point P is a point m away from A and n away from B.' Bottom: A(a), B(b), Q on the line, with a large arc m from A to Q and a small arc n from B to Q; caption 'Point Q is a point m away from A and n away from B.'

items.quote: Regarding the line segment AB connecting two points A(a) and B(b)
items.text: Regarding the line segment AB connecting two points A(a) and B(b) on a number line:

items.quote: The coordinate of point P dividing segment AB internally in the ratio
items.claim: (i) The coordinate of P dividing AB internally in the ratio m : n is P((na + mb)/(m + n)).

items.quote: The coordinate of point Q dividing segment AB externally in the ratio
items.claim: (ii) The coordinate of Q dividing AB externally in the ratio m : n is Q((−na + mb)/(m − n)).

items.quote: Be careful with the order of multiplication (cross-multiply).
items.claim: Side note beside formulas (i) and (ii): shows (na+mb)/(m+n) and (−na+mb)/(m−n); be careful with the order of multiplication (cross-multiply).

items.quote: The coordinate of the midpoint M is (since it divides segment AB
items.claim: (iii) The coordinate of the midpoint M (dividing AB internally in 1:1) is M((a+b)/2).

items.text: Subterranean Research Lab Infrastructure. A team of marine biologists is operating an underwater research habitat anchored along a straight vertical trench wall. Currently, two primary monitoring pods are anchored directly to the trench wall: Pod A is positioned at a depth of −8 km. Pod B is positioned closer to the surface at a depth of −3 km. items.quote: Let the coordinates of point P be (s, 0).
items.stem: Find P on the x-axis equidistant from A(−2, 1) and B(3, 4).
solution: Let the coordinates of point P be $(s, 0)$.
Since it is equidistant from 2 points A(−2, 1) and B(3, 4), $AP = BP$
Simplifying and solving this gives $s = 2$
Therefore, the required coordinates is P(2, 0).

items.caption: Coordinate axes with points A(−2, 1) in the second quadrant, B(3, 4) in the first quadrant, and P(s, 0) on the x-axis; segments AP and BP drawn with equal-length tick marks.

items.quote: Let the coordinates of point Q be (s, 2s−1).
items.stem: Find Q on y = 2x − 1 equidistant from A(1, 4) and B(3, 1).
solution: Let the coordinates of point Q be $(s, 2s-1)$.
Since it is equidistant from 2 points A(1, 4) and B(3, 1), $AQ = BQ$
Simplifying and solving this gives $s=\frac{13}{8}$
Since the required point is on y= 2x−1, Q(13/8, 9/4)

solution: (a) $\left(\frac{2\times3+1\times(-2)}{1+2},\frac{2\times7+1\times(-3)}{1+2}\right)$, so $P\left(\frac43,\frac{11}{3}\right)$
(b) $\left(\frac{-3\times3+1\times5}{1-3},\frac{-3\times7+1\times2}{1-3}\right)$, so $Q\left(2,\frac{19}{2}\right)$
(c) $\left(\frac{5+(-2)}{2},\frac{2+(-3)}{2}\right)$, so $M\left(\frac32,-\frac12\right)$

items.quote: Find the coordinates of point B symmetric to point A( − 3, 2)
items.stem: Find the coordinates of point B symmetric to point A$(-3,2)$ with respect to point P$(2,6)$.
solution: Let the coordinates of point B be $(s, t)$.
The coordinates of the midpoint of segment AB can be expressed as $\left(\frac{-3+s}{2}, \frac{2+t}{2}\right)$.
Since this coincides with point P(2, 6): $\frac{-3+s}{2}=2$ and $\frac{2+t}{2}=6$.
Solving this gives $s = 7, t = 10$.
